name: Present Simple
description: Habits, routines, facts and repeated actions.

name: Present Continuous
description: Actions happening now or around the current period.

examples.negative: I am not reading a book.
examples.question: Are you reading a book?

name: Present Perfect
description: Past actions connected with the present or unfinished time periods.

examples.negative: I have not finished my work.
examples.question: Have you finished your work?

name: Present Perfect Continuous
description: An activity that started in the past and continues or has a visible recent result.

examples.positive: I have been waiting for you.
examples.negative: I have not been waiting for long.
examples.question: Have you been waiting for me?

examples.negative: I did not love the movie.
examples.question: Did you love the movie?

name: Past Continuous
description: An action that was in progress at a particular past time.

name: Past Perfect
description: An action completed before another past action.

examples.positive: I had finished the report before lunch.
examples.negative: I had not finished the report before lunch.
examples.question: Had you finished the report before lunch?

name: Past Perfect Continuous
description: An activity that continued up to a point in the past.

examples.positive: I had been waiting for an hour.
examples.negative: I had not been waiting for an hour.
examples.question: Had you been waiting for an hour?

examples.negative: I will not call you tomorrow.
examples.question: Will you call me tomorrow?

name: Future Continuous
description: An action that will be in progress at a future time.

examples.positive: I will be working tomorrow morning.
examples.negative: I will not be working tomorrow morning.
examples.question: Will you be working tomorrow morning?

name: Future Perfect
description: An action that will be completed before a future point.

examples.positive: I will have finished the report by Friday.
examples.negative: I will not have finished the report by Friday.
examples.question: Will you have finished the report by Friday?

name: Future Perfect Continuous
description: An activity continuing up to a future point.

examples.positive: I will have been working here for a year by June.
examples.negative: I will not have been working here for a year by June.
examples.question: Will you have been working here for a year by June?
